subject.title: docs: add async cross-Gateway agent handoff option

question: Should OpenClaw’s core documentation recommend AgentPost by name as the asynchronous cross-Gateway handoff path, rather than describe a vendor-neutral pattern or route the integration to its owner surface?
rationale: This is a documentation and trust-boundary choice: the answer determines whether OpenClaw should direct users to a third-party hosted service that receives agent traffic and uses receiver credentials.

options.title: Use vendor-neutral guidance
options.body: Describe the asynchronous polling pattern and the existing Gateway/webhook constraints without recommending an unaudited hosted provider.

options.title: Approve a named integration
options.body: Keep the named recommendation only after maintainer approval and verification of its API contract, data handling, credentials, support ownership, and lifecycle.

options.title: Route it outside core docs
options.body: Ask the service owner to publish a maintained plugin, skill, or integration guide rather than placing provider-specific operational guidance in core documentation.

recommendation.title: Use vendor-neutral guidance
recommendation.body: Describe the asynchronous polling pattern and the existing Gateway/webhook constraints without recommending an unaudited hosted provider.

likelyOwner.reason: They can clarify the intended scope and supply vendor-contract evidence, although an established current-main documentation owner was not available in the review evidence.
